AlternateTargets: mote after mote, land after land
Senses.Explanation: Literally, “every mote and every land”: the repeated nouns make the phrase distributive. Across 205 occurrences in 116 allowlisted texts, Chan masters pair it with “each thing and each particular” (物物頭頭), say that every mote and land “fully displays” (全彰), and place it in public addresses as the range of an action or disclosure. One address says, “every mote and every land once manifested awe-inspiring light; each thing and each particular fully displayed the true eye” (塵塵剎剎，曾現威光。物物頭頭，全彰正眼). Another gives the compact parallel, “each thing and each particular—the whole body; every mote and every land—the great function” (物物頭頭全身，塵塵剎剎大用). The phrase is also made a test: “if you understand, every mote and every land; if you do not, a kick to the head” (若也會得，塵塵剎剎；若也不會，當頭一蹋). The corpus thus bends a cosmological distributive into recurring teaching-seat language for an all-pervading range; this entry makes no claim beyond those deployments.
Senses.Note: No second referent was found. Reversal as “land after land, mote after mote” (剎剎塵塵) changes order, not the thing denoted.

Occurrences.Kwic: 塵塵剎剎，曾現威光。物物頭頭，全彰正眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of the Ancestral Guidelines (列祖提綱錄): the unlabeled continuation of Ying'an Tanhua's imperial-birthday hall addresses says that every dust and every land has displayed majestic radiance and every thing fully manifests the true eye.

Occurrences.Kwic: 物物頭頭全身。塵塵剎剎大用。
所謂一處通，處處通，塵塵剎剎盡歸宗。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan (隱元禪師語錄), Yinyuan Longqi's Huangbo Mountain record. In a memorial hall address, Yinyuan Longqi says that when one place opens through, every place opens through, and every mote and every land returns to the source.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若也會得，塵塵剎剎；若也不會，當頭一蹋。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Lamp Compendium of Qiannan (黔南會燈錄): in his Buddha-birthday hall address, Xiangya Ting says understanding means dust after dust and land after land, while not understanding earns a frontal kick.

Occurrences.Kwic: 塵塵剎剎，剎剎塵塵是我，我是剎剎塵塵，誰見塵塵剎剎？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings (御選語錄): in the Yuanming Layman's recorded discourse, the Yongzheng Emperor says that dust after dust and land after land are himself, that he is every dust and land, and asks who sees them.
